opening_hours.notes: Special exhibits may have extended hours.

places.place_tip: Check out the fossil collection and the historic library.

places.name: Amsterdamse Poort
places.ai_summary: The last remaining city gate of Haarlem, offering a glimpse into the city's medieval past.
places.place_tip: Great spot for photos with the gate and canal.

places.name: Windmill De Adriaan
places.ai_summary: A historic windmill and museum offering panoramic views of Haarlem and its surroundings.
places.place_tip: Climb to the top for the best views of Haarlem.

places.name: Haarlem Canal Cruise
places.ai_summary: A relaxing cruise on the canals of Haarlem, offering a unique perspective of the city’s historic architecture.

opening_hours.notes: Advance booking recommended in peak season.

places.place_tip: Enjoy the illuminated bridges and buildings during the cruise.

places.name: Corrie ten Boom House
places.ai_summary: The hiding place of Jewish families during WWII, now a museum dedicated to Corrie ten Boom and the Dutch resistance.

opening_hours.notes: Guided tours only, book in advance.

places.place_tip: Visit the museum shop for books and souvenirs.

attribution.description: Corrie ten Boom in scouting uniform (around 1921). The triangle on her uniform refers to the name of the scouting group: "the triangle girls".

places.name: Haarlemmerhout Park
places.ai_summary: The oldest public park in the Netherlands, featuring beautiful gardens, walking paths, and a petting zoo.

opening_hours.notes: Best time to visit is during the spring bloom.

places.place_tip: Check out the historic trees and the small observatory.

attribution.title: Haarlemmerhout
attribution.author: Original uploader was Jane023 at en.wikipedia
attribution.description: photo of Haarlemmerhout, oldest public park in the Netherlands. Since the middle ages open to the public, it wasn't designed as a park for recreational use until 1756, when the landscape designer Jan van Vorel introduced the French garden system of straight lines and star-shaped woods, still to be found in the lines of the park today.
